title: uPVC Column Pipe Buying Guide for Submersible Pumps and Borewells
metaTitle: uPVC Column Pipe Buying Guide for Borewell Pumps | Prayag
description: Choose a uPVC column pipe for a submersible pump by borewell depth, pump HP, pressure class, pipe size, thread design and installation conditions.
bodyHtml:
Quick answer

A uPVC column pipe should be selected from the pump and borewell data, not by pipe diameter alone. Confirm the total installation depth, pump horsepower, delivery head, pipe size, pressure requirement, thread or joint design, water quality and lifting method. The final specification should be approved by the pump supplier or qualified borewell installer. Buyers can then compare available options in the Prayag uPVC column pipe range.

Column pipes form the rising main that carries water from a submersible pump to the surface. They also support the suspended pump assembly, so they face internal pressure, tensile load and installation stress at the same time. A mismatch may lead to joint failure, leakage, difficult retrieval or loss of performance.

Information to collect before asking for a quotation

InputWhat to recordWhy it matters
Borewell depthTotal depth and static/dynamic water levelsHelps estimate suspended length and operating head
Pump detailsBrand, model, HP, stages and outlet sizeDefines flow, head and connection needs
Required dischargeExpected litres per minute or application demandSupports correct hydraulic sizing
Pipe sizeNominal size compatible with pump and flowAffects friction loss and fit
Pressure classManufacturer-recommended class for the dutyRelates to internal pressure and depth
Joint designCoupler or belling arrangement and thread detailsAffects assembly and load transfer
Water qualitySand, minerals, corrosive content and temperatureInfluences material and maintenance planning
Installation methodManual or mechanical lowering and retrievalAffects handling and tools

Understand what a column pipe does

A column pipe carries pumped water upward while hanging vertically inside the borewell. The joints must transfer the weight of the pump, cable and pipe string. During starting and stopping, the system may also experience changes in pressure and load. This is why ordinary plumbing pipe should not be substituted simply because the diameter appears similar.

1. Borewell depth and pump setting depth

Use the actual pump setting depth, not only the drilled depth of the borewell. The pump is normally installed below the operating water level but above the bottom to avoid sediment intake. The column pipe length is based on that installation position plus the above-ground connection arrangement.

Greater depth increases suspended load and may increase pressure requirements. Do not select a deeper-duty system by guessing from a neighbouring borewell because water level and pump configuration can differ even within the same area.

2. Pump horsepower, head and discharge

Horsepower is useful but not enough on its own. Two pumps with similar HP can have different stage configurations, discharge and head. Obtain the pump performance data and operating point. The pipe must be compatible with the pump outlet and intended flow without creating excessive friction loss.

The installer should consider total dynamic head, which includes vertical lift, delivery pressure and friction. Oversimplifying the calculation can reduce water delivery or place unnecessary load on the pump.

3. Select the correct pipe size

Pipe size should match the pump outlet and hydraulic requirement. An undersized rising main increases velocity and friction loss. An unnecessarily oversized pipe may add cost and may not match the pump or borewell clearance. Check the outer diameter against casing size, cable position and any centralizers or safety devices.

4. Pressure class is a design decision

Pressure class should be selected according to the system duty and manufacturer guidance. The pressure near the pump can be significantly higher than the pressure at the surface because of the water column and pump head. Starting conditions and closed-valve operation may also affect pressure.

Do not compare two pipes only by wall thickness without understanding their intended classification, material and joint system. Use published technical data and get written confirmation for the planned depth and pump.

5. Coupler type and belling type joints

Column pipes may use different connection formats. In a coupler-type system, separate couplers join the pipe lengths. In a belling-type system, the socket or bell is integrated into the pipe end. Each design has its own assembly method and tool requirements. The entire pipe string should use compatible components from the same specified system.

Threads must be clean and protected from damage during transport. Installers should follow the recommended engagement and tightening method rather than using uncontrolled force. Incorrect assembly can damage threads or create misalignment.

6. Tensile load and pump retrieval

The pipe string carries the suspended load. Consider the pump weight, water-filled pipe weight, cable and accessories. Retrieval can create additional stress if the pipe is pulled unevenly or if the pump is stuck. Use suitable lifting clamps and support equipment. Never hold or lower the entire assembly by the electrical cable.

7. Water quality and borewell conditions

Record whether the water carries sand, silt or high mineral content. Sand can affect the pump and flow system, while deposits can influence long-term performance. Water quality should be tested where the supply is intended for drinking or sensitive industrial use. The pipe choice is only one part of a safe water system.

8. Verify casing and bore clearance

Confirm that the pump, column pipe, cable and accessories fit within the bore casing with adequate clearance. Buyers planning a new borewell should also review the available uPVC pipe category and obtain professional guidance on casing and related pipes rather than mixing unverified components.

Restricted clearance can make lowering difficult and increase the risk of rubbing or cable damage. It can also complicate retrieval. The borewell should be straight and properly developed before the pump assembly is installed.

Installation procedure: practical checkpoints

  • Inspect every pipe length, thread and joint before lowering.
  • Keep threads clean and use only the specified sealing or assembly method.
  • Support each section with proper clamps during joining.
  • Secure the power cable at recommended intervals without overtightening.
  • Lower the assembly steadily and prevent impact with the casing.
  • Maintain an accurate record of installed lengths and pump depth.
  • Connect the top assembly with correct support, valves and delivery piping.
  • Test discharge, current draw, pressure and leakage after commissioning.

Delivery line and water storage planning

The rising main connects to the above-ground delivery system, which may feed a farm line, overhead tank or process. Size and route this line independently according to flow and distance. Where the borewell fills a tank, coordinate the pump controls with the Prayag storage tank range and provide overflow, level control and safe support.

Electrical and safety considerations

A qualified electrician should size the cable, starter, protection and earthing for the pump. Dry-run protection and suitable control logic can reduce the risk of pump damage when the water level falls. Electrical joints exposed to moisture must use appropriate waterproofing. Mechanical pipe selection cannot compensate for unsafe electrical work.

How to compare quotations

Ask each supplier to quote the same specification: size, pressure class, joint type, length, quantity, accessories and installation scope. Confirm whether lifting tools, clamps, top adapters, transport and commissioning are included. A cheaper per-metre rate may produce a higher total cost if critical components are excluded.

Request product identification and technical literature. Avoid combining pipe lengths or couplers from unrelated systems unless the manufacturers explicitly confirm compatibility. Consistency makes assembly, responsibility and future service easier.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Selecting only by pump HP and ignoring head or depth.
  • Using the drilled bore depth instead of the actual pump setting depth.
  • Choosing ordinary plumbing pipe for a suspended pump application.
  • Mixing incompatible threads, couplers or pipe classes.
  • Damaging threads during transport and still installing them.
  • Lowering or retrieving the pump without proper clamps.
  • Failing to account for casing clearance and cable routing.
  • Ignoring pressure testing, electrical protection or water quality.

Maintenance and retrieval planning

Keep the borewell completion record, pump invoice and pipe specification together. Record the number and length of pipe sections installed. This information helps when the pump must be removed for servicing. Inspect each section during retrieval and replace any part with damaged threads, deformation or other visible issues rather than reinstalling it automatically.

Frequently asked questions

Can I select a column pipe only from pump horsepower?

No. HP must be considered with pump head, discharge, installation depth, pipe size and pressure class.

Are uPVC column pipes the same as regular uPVC plumbing pipes?

No. Column pipes are designed as rising mains for submersible pump installations and have specific load and joint requirements.

Which is better: coupler type or belling type?

The better choice depends on the manufacturer’s system, depth, installation practice and available tools. Use a complete compatible system rather than mixing formats.

How do I know the required pressure class?

Use the pump performance data, installation depth and manufacturer selection guidance. The installer or engineer should confirm the final class.

Should a safety rope be used?

Follow the pump and installation guidance. Any safety support must be suitable for the load and must not replace correct pipe assembly or lifting practices.

Final buying checklist

  • Borewell and pump-setting depths recorded.
  • Pump curve, HP, head, discharge and outlet size available.
  • Pipe size and pressure class approved for the duty.
  • Joint format and accessories are fully compatible.
  • Casing clearance and cable routing checked.
  • Water quality and sand conditions considered.
  • Installation tools and trained crew arranged.
  • Top support, delivery line and controls planned.
  • Product and installation records will be retained.

Once the technical specification is approved, compare suitable products on the Prayag uPVC Column Pipes page. For product availability or project support, visit Contact Prayag.

Commissioning checks after installation

After the pump is lowered and connected, commissioning should be treated as a separate stage rather than a quick switch-on. Confirm the pump rotation where applicable, measure discharge, observe delivery pressure and compare motor current with the pump data. A major difference between expected and actual flow may indicate incorrect pump selection, a restricted line, leakage, excessive friction or a water-level issue.

Run the system long enough to observe stable operation. Check the top connection, valves and delivery line for movement or leakage. Listen for unusual vibration and confirm that the electrical protection does not trip. Record the readings so future service teams have a baseline. Where water is intended for consumption, flush the system and arrange appropriate testing before use.

Troubleshooting signs that need attention

Low discharge is not always caused by the column pipe. It can result from falling water level, worn pump stages, voltage problems, a partially closed valve, leakage at a joint or an undersized delivery line. Repeated pump cycling may point to control or storage issues. Air, sand or irregular flow should be investigated promptly rather than accepted as normal.

If the system loses pressure after shutdown, check the non-return arrangement and visible connections. Do not pull the pump immediately without basic diagnosis, because retrieval itself is a significant operation. When removal is required, use the installation record to prepare the correct clamps, lifting capacity and workspace.

Supplier and installer questions to ask

Ask the supplier to identify the exact pipe series, size, pressure class, joint type and recommended depth range for the stated pump. Ask whether the quoted couplers, adapters and top fittings belong to the same system. Request written installation instructions and clarify warranty conditions, especially any requirement for trained installation.

Ask the installer how the string will be supported during assembly, how cable will be secured, how threads will be protected and how installed depth will be recorded. A professional answer should refer to tools and procedures, not only experience. Clear responsibility between pump supplier, pipe supplier and installer reduces disputes if the system does not perform as expected.
